'''Dalibor Bagarić''' (born 7 February 1980)<ref name=bbr>{{Cite web|title=Dalibor Bagarić NBA Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bagarda01.html|accessdate=17 September 2025|website=[[Basketball Reference]]|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|language=en}}</ref> is a Croatian former professional [[basketball]] player. He had a stint with the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]'s [[Chicago Bulls]] from 2000 to 2003.

==Professional career==
A {{convert|7|ft|1|in|m|adj=on}} [[Center (basketball)|center]] born in [[Munich]], [[West Germany]], Bagarić had averaged 18.3 points and 10.4 rebounds per game for the Croatian team [[Benston Zagreb]] before the Bulls selected him with the 24th pick in the [[2000 NBA draft]]. Bagarić never averaged more than 2.6 points and 2.5 rebounds per game during his time with the Bulls.

He returned to Europe after the Bulls bought out his contract in 2003, and began playing for the Greek club [[Olympiacos BC|Olympiacos]]. He played only 10 games with the Bulls during the 2002 - 2003 season, with his final NBA game ever being on 15 April 2003 in a 115 - 106 win over the Philadelphia 76ers. Bagarić played for 3 minutes and the only stat he recorded was 2 points.

In 2004, he moved to Italian club [[Climamio Bologna|Fortitudo Bologna]]. In the summer of 2006, he transferred to [[CB Girona]] of the Spanish [[Asociación de Clubs de Baloncesto|ACB]] league.
In September 2007 he returned to Fortitudo Bologna after signing on a one-year contract.<ref>[http://www.ulebcup.com/ulebcup/home/news/i/15259/448/item Fortitudo brings back Bagaric – News – Welcome to ULEB Cup<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20130205060628/http://www.ulebcup.com/ulebcup/home/news/i/15259/448/item |date=2013-02-05 }}</ref> In November 2010 he signed with [[Maroussi B.C.|Maroussi]].<ref>[https://grbasket.blogspot.com/2010/11/blog-post_3096.html ΜΑΡΟΥΣΙ | Ψήλωσε με Μπαγκαριτς...] {{in lang|el}}</ref> At the beginning of the 2011–12 season, Bagarić signed with [[CB Valladolid]], but left the club in late November, returning to Croatia and signing with [[KK Cedevita|Cedevita]]. In September 2012, he signed a one-month deal with [[Sporting Al Riyadi Beirut]] in Lebanon.<ref>[https://www.asia-basket.com/Lebanon/basketball.aspx?NewsID=289838 Sporting Al Riyadi Beirut signs 1-month deal with Dalibor Bagaric]</ref> In December 2012, he signed with the Lebanese club [[Amchit Club|Amchit]]. In the 2013–14 season, he played for [[Étoile Sportive du Sahel (basketball)|Étoile Sportive du Sahel]] in Tunisia,  [[KK Zabok]] in Croatia and Al-Ahli Benghazi in Libya.<ref>[http://www.invictussportsgroup.com/news_1864_Croatia,+BAGARI%C4%86+back+to+Zabok+%26... Croatia, BAGARIĆ back to Zabok &...] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304071229/http://www.invictussportsgroup.com/news_1864_Croatia%2C+BAGARI%C4%86+back+to+Zabok+%26... |date=2016-03-04 }}</ref> In 2014, he signed with [[Brose Baskets|Brose Baskets Bamberg]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] where he signed, on 2 December 2014, a contract extension.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/143287/brose-baskets-bamberg-extends-dalibor-bagaric-for-the-season.html Brose Baskets Bamberg extends Dalibor Bagaric for the season]</ref>

On 9 June 2016 Bagarić announced his retirement.<ref>{{cite web|title=Croatian big man Dalibor Bagaric retires at 36|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/croatia/201721/croatian-big-man-dalibor-bagaric-retires-at-36.html|publisher=Sportando|date=10 June 2016|access-date=10 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160808151256/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/croatia/201721/croatian-big-man-dalibor-bagaric-retires-at-36.html|archive-date=8 August 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==National team career==
With the junior national teams of Croatia, Bagarić won the gold medal at the [[1996 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]].

He was also a member of the senior [[Croatian national basketball team]]. He has played at the [[EuroBasket 2003]] and [[EuroBasket 2005]].
